Okay, so I need to figure out which statement about rocks is true. The options are A) Minerals are made of rocks., B) Crystals are made of rocks., C) Rocks are made of one or more minerals., and D) Magma is made of solid rock.

First, I'll start by understanding each term. Rocks are a major part of the Earth's crust, and they can be made up of different materials. I remember that minerals are the building blocks of rocks, so maybe that relates to option C. But wait, option C says rocks are made of one or more minerals. I think that's correct because rocks are aggregates of minerals. So C might be true.

Now, looking at the other options. Option A says minerals are made of rocks. That doesn't make sense because minerals are the building blocks, not the other way around. So A is false.

Option B says crystals are made of rocks. Crystals are actually a type of mineral, so they can't be made from rocks. That makes B false too.

Option D says magma is made of solid rock. Magma is molten, so it's not solid. Instead, magma can contain crystals and other materials suspended within it, but it's not made of solid rock. So D is also false.

Wait, but I thought C was correct. Rocks are made of minerals, so C should be true. But in the initial analysis, the planner said D was true. That must be a mistake. So the error was in thinking that magma is made of solid rock, which isn't the case.

So the mistake was made by the planner in step 1, where they incorrectly concluded that D was true. The reason is that they misunderstood the composition of magma, thinking it's solid rock, when in fact it's molten.
</think>

Reason for Mistake: The Planner incorrectly concluded that magma is made of solid rock, which is false. Magma is molten and not solid. This mistake was made due to a misunderstanding of magma's composition.
